# 2 Baruch Chapter 17 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Syriac MS (Codex Ambrosianus 7a1) | **Section:** First Fast and Vision

---

**1** And I answered and said: "O Lord, lo! You have announced to us the shortness of the time that has passed and the length of the time to come.

**2** And you have shown us that this present age is short and painful, but the future age is long and desirable.

**3** What have we profited by this, seeing that we came into the world in great suffering, and that we live only to be saddened all our days?

**4** But you have shown us that the adversary has had dominion over us. But Adam first sinned and brought death upon all those who were not of his time."

---

*LOGOS notes: Baruch continues the theodicy dialogue. V.4 is the critical Adamic theology: Adam's sin brought death, but the text carefully stops short of blaming all individuals for Adam's sin — that elaboration comes in ch.19. "Adversary" = the satan/ha-satan figure.*
